title: Keep encounter order where it matters in a parallel stream

blocks.text: A parallel stream processes its chunks on several threads at once, so any step that hands elements to the outside world, or picks one of them, must say whether encounter order matters. `forEach` and `findAny` do not keep it; `forEachOrdered` and `findFirst` do, at the cost of some coordination between the threads.
Write two static methods in `OrderedOutput`. Each receives a stream that may be sequential or parallel:

items: `void emitInOrder(Stream<String> lines, Consumer<String> sink)`: hands every line to `sink`, in encounter order.
`Optional<Integer> firstAbove(Stream<Integer> numbers, int threshold)`: the first number, in encounter order, that is greater than `threshold`.

blocks.text: The tests also hand both methods large parallel streams, where many numbers are above the threshold.

cases.says: It emits every line in order and finds the first number above the threshold in a sequential stream.
A parallel stream's lines reach the sink in encounter order: forEach hands them over in whatever order the threads run.
On a parallel stream the match returned is the first in encounter order: findAny returns whichever thread finds one first.

concepts: findFirst keeps encounter order in parallel, while findAny returns whichever match a thread finds first.
forEach on a parallel stream follows no order; forEachOrdered keeps encounter order.
